      duties of kings, as promulgated by Manu, fraught with crookedness and
      unfairness and precepts opposed to tranquillity and virtue. Why dost thou
      then, O king, forgive the wicked sons of Dhritarashtra? Thou hast
      intelligence, prowess, learning and high birth. Why dost thou then, O
      tiger among men, act in respect of thy duties, like a huge snake that is
      destitute of motion? O son of Kunti, he that desireth to conceal us, only
      wisheth to conceal the mountains of Himavat by means of a handful of

      spreading branches and flowers and leaves, or like Indra’s elephant, how
      will Jishnu live unknown? How also will these children, the brothers,
      Nakula and Sahadeva, equal unto a couple of young lions, both live in

      world, live unknown? Me also, everybody knoweth from my boyhood. I do not
      see how I can live unknown. As well mighty mountains of Meru be sought to

      kingdom. These kings and princes will all follow the bad son of
